questions.question: Rajiv invested a certain sum of money at 10% per annum. After 2 years, he received ₹199.5 as compound interest, compounded annually. Find the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) for 2 years at the same rate.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of **Compound Interest** for 2 years at 10% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 21%.

Effective rate of **Simple Interest** for 2 years at 10% = 10 × 2 = 20%.

Given that 21% equivalent = ₹199.5.

Then 20% equivalent = (199.5 ÷ 21) × 20 = 9.5 × 20 = 190.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹190.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given**: **Compound Interest (CI)** = ₹199.5, **Rate (R)** = 10%, **Time (T)** = 2 years.

**Formula Used**: CI = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)T − 1] and SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3f28c322ee6d114518b672f6d69609497498888812e2bcf226af42cdbc318a4.png] 

⇒ 199.5 = P[(1 + 10 ÷ 100)² − 1]

⇒ 199.5 = P[(1.1)² − 1]

⇒ 199.5 = P[1.21 − 1]

⇒ 199.5 = 0.21 × P

⇒ P = 199.5 ÷ 0.21 = 950

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = (950 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ **SI** = 19000 ÷ 100 = 190

**∴ The correct answer is ₹190.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate for 2 Years

For a rate R%, the effective **Compound Interest** rate for 2 years is given by R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** for 2 years is CI − SI = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Relationship for 2 Years

The ratio of **CI** to **SI** for 2 years is CI ÷ SI = (200 + R) ÷ 200.

questions.question: Priyal is 5 years younger than her brother. After 4 years, the sum of their ages will be 39 years. What is Priyal's current age?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of **current ages** = 39 − (2 persons × 4 years) = 31 years.

Age difference between **Priyal** and her **brother** = 5 years.

**Priyal's current age** (younger) = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (31 − 5) ÷ 2 = 13 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between **Priyal** and **brother** = 5 years.

Sum of ages after **4 years** = 39 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a0b94c8a8c51d176028c051727b68061dcb68a59192a76d5dd9f04486ded9f6.png] 

Let **Priyal's current age** be x years.

Then, her **brother's current age** = (x + 5) years.

⇒ After 4 years, Priyal's age = (x + 4) years.

⇒ After 4 years, brother's age = (x + 5 + 4) = (x + 9) years.

⇒ (x + 4) + (x + 9) = 39

⇒ 2x + 13 = 39

⇒ 2x = 39 − 13

⇒ 2x = 26

⇒ x = 26 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 13 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** over time. If Priyal is 5 years younger today, she will remain 5 years younger throughout her life.

Sum of Ages Rule

If the sum of ages of 'n' people is 'S' now, then the sum of their ages after 'T' years will be S + (n × T).

Calculation of Individual Ages

When the Sum (S) and Difference (D) of two ages are known: Younger Age = (S − D) ÷ 2 and Older Age = (S + D) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 27 and 324, respectively. If one number is 81, find the other number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Product of two numbers** is always equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**.

Second Number = (**HCF × LCM**) ÷ **First Number**

Second Number = (**27 × 324**) ÷ **81**

Second Number = **324 ÷ 3** = **108**

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**HCF** of two numbers = 27

**LCM** of two numbers = 324

**First number** (n₁) = 81

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b872e381787727120cb0084cfec781d05e686170c4e92f8b9b7af1411914e86.png] 

**Formula Used:**

n₁ × n₂ = HCF × LCM

**Calculations:**

⇒ 81 × n₂ = 27 × 324

⇒ n₂ = (27 × 324) ÷ 81

⇒ n₂ = 1 × 324 ÷ 3

⇒ n₂ = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Property

For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

HCF and LCM Relation

The HCF of a given set of numbers is always a factor of their LCM.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, their HCF is 1 and their LCM is simply their product.

questions.question: Find the positive integral value of x if the fourth proportional of x, x + 1, 2x + 3 is y and y = 3x + 3.

questions.question: A string initially in the shape of a circle with a radius of 21 cm is cut into two distinct pieces. The first piece is reshaped into a rectangle where the length is twice its breadth, while the second piece is formed into a square. If the perimeter of the rectangle is 24 cm greater than the perimeter of the square, find the breadth of the rectangle. [Use π = 22/7]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total string length = Circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 21 = 132 cm.

Let **Perimeter of Rectangle** be PR and **Perimeter of Square** be PS.

PR + PS = 132 and PR − PS = 24.

Solving for PR: PR = (132 + 24) ÷ 2 = 78 cm.

For rectangle, 2(2B + B) = 78 ⇒ 6B = 78 ⇒ B = 13 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** of circle (r) = 21 cm

**Rectangle:** Length (L) = 2 × Breadth (B)

**Condition:** Perimeter of rectangle = Perimeter of square + 24 cm

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of **Circle** = 2πr

Perimeter of **Rectangle** = 2(L + B)

Perimeter of **Square** = 4 × Side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b621ef95a6772138be28b353a5e3f95b568da6c088b79369f1421dc4e0054a34.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length of the string = 2 × (22/7) × 21

⇒ Total length = 2 × 22 × 3 = 132 cm

⇒ Let Perimeter of **Rectangle** = PR and Perimeter of **Square** = PS

⇒ PR + PS = 132 ---(i)

⇒ PR − PS = 24 ---(ii)

⇒ Adding (i) and (ii): 2PR = 156

⇒ PR = 78 cm

⇒ Since L = 2B, Perimeter PR = 2(2B + B) = 6B

⇒ 6B = 78

⇒ B = 78 ÷ 6 = 13 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circumference and Area of Circle

Circumference = 2πr and Area = πr², where r is the radius of the circle.

Perimeter of Polygons

Perimeter is the total length of the boundary. Rectangle = 2(l + b), Square = 4a, Triangle = sum of all three sides.

Conservation of Length

When a wire/string is reshaped, its **total length** remains constant and is equal to the sum of the perimeters of the new shapes.

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 45%, 50% and 25% in three successive months, but increases by 65% in the fourth month. What is the percentage decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Round off to 2 decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net multiplying factor = 0.55 × 0.50 × 0.75 × 1.65

Net multiplier = 0.3403125

**Percentage decrease** = (1 − 0.3403125) × 100 = 65.96875%

Rounding to 2 decimal places, we get 65.97%.

**∴ The correct answer is 65.97%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Successive changes in **fuel price**: −45%, −50%, −25% (decreases) and +65% (increase).

**Formula Used:**

Final Price = Initial Price × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100) × (1 ± r₃/100) × (1 ± r₄/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/367f6a231394a0c1c0d3edfb1ac85f07d8b70783970c14ff365cd39037a02b80.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **original price** of fuel be 100 units.

⇒ Price after 1st month = 100 × (1 − 45/100) = 100 × 0.55 = 55

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd month = 55 × (1 − 50/100) = 55 × 0.5 = 27.5

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 27.5 × (1 − 25/100) = 27.5 × 0.75 = 20.625

⇒ Price after 4th month = 20.625 × (1 + 65/100) = 20.625 × 1.65 = 34.03125

⇒ Net decrease in price = 100 − 34.03125 = 65.96875

⇒ **Percentage decrease** = (65.96875 / 100) × 100 = 65.96875%

⇒ Required percentage ≈ 65.97%

**∴ The correct answer is 65.97%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a%, then b%, then c%... the final multiplier is (1 + a/100) × (1 + b/100) × (1 + c/100)... where positive is increase and negative is decrease.

Net Change Formula

For two successive changes a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.

Rounding Rule

If the third decimal digit is 5 or more, round up the second decimal digit. Here, 65.968... becomes 65.97.

questions.question: If the simple interest on a sum of ₹9,800 is ₹16,562 for a period of 13 years, find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 1 year = 16562 ÷ 13 = ₹1274

Rate % = (Interest per year ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (1274 ÷ 9800) × 100

Rate % = 1274 ÷ 98 = 13%

**∴ The correct answer is 13%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹9,800**

Simple Interest (SI) = **₹16,562**

Time (T) = **13 years**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/45a09ab1f8eb2ab9012f8221ba91ab613a8ac5b860b5ca92e509c45138bdacd2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 16562 = (9800 × R × 13) ÷ 100

⇒ 16562 = 98 × R × 13

⇒ 16562 = 1274 × R

⇒ R = 16562 ÷ 1274

⇒ R = 13%

**∴ The correct answer is 13%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

The basic formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. From this, the **Rate of Interest** can be derived as R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).

Total Amount

The **Total Amount (A)** at the end of the period is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Simple Interest**: A = P + SI.

Nature of Simple Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the interest earned remains constant every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal** amount.

questions.question: The cost of an article is increased by 20% in the first year. In the second year the increased cost is decreased by 24%. If the final cost of the article is ₹1,938, find the original cost of the article.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective percentage change = 20 − 24 − (20 × 24)/100 = −8.8%

Final cost as percentage of original = 100% − 8.8% = 91.2%

Given that 91.2% = ₹1,938

Original cost (100%) = (1,938 ÷ 91.2) × 100 = ₹2,125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f58b634c0eb48d9de721f7b773e92ff1185a03f908b802e60085d407ea98e0a4.png]

⇒ Let the **original cost** of the article be ₹x.

⇒ After 24% **decrease** on the increased cost, final cost = 1.2x × (1 − 24/100)

⇒ 1,938 = 0.912x

⇒ x = 1,938 ÷ 0.912

⇒ x = 2,125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,125.**

Successive Percentage Change Formula

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%. Use positive for increase and negative for decrease.

Multiplying Factor Method

For an increase of r%, multiply by (1 + r/100). For a decrease of r%, multiply by (1 − r/100).

Reverse Percentage Calculation

To find the original value when the final value and percentage change are known: Original Value = Final Value ÷ (Net Multiplying Factor).

questions.question: Evaluate 23³ + (-11)³ + (-12)³
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the sum: 23 + (−11) + (−12) = 23 − 23 = **0**.

Using the **conditional identity**: If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = **3abc**.

Result = 3 × 23 × (−11) × (−12) = 69 × 132 = **9108**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** a = 23, b = −11, c = −12

**Formula Used:** a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ First, evaluate the sum of the terms: **a + b + c**

⇒ 23 + (−11) + (−12) = 23 − 11 − 12 = 0

⇒ Since **a + b + c = 0**, the entire right-hand side of the formula becomes zero.

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 0 × (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) = 0

⇒ Therefore, a³ + b³ + c³ = **3abc**

⇒ 23³ + (−11)³ + (−12)³ = 3 × 23 × (−11) × (−12)

⇒ 3 × 23 × 132 = 69 × 132 = 9108

**∴ The correct answer is 9108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Special Case of Cubic Identity

When the sum of three variables is zero, the identity **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc** simplifies complex cubic calculations into simple multiplication.

Alternative Form of Identity

The expression **a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca** can also be written as **½ [(a−b)² + (b−c)² + (c−a)²]**, which is always non-negative for real numbers.

BODMAS Rule in Simplification

Always resolve **brackets** and **orders** (powers) before addition or multiplication unless an identity is applicable.

questions.question: A stationery shop sells notebooks and pens. The cost of 4 notebooks and 6 pens is ₹228. The cost of 7 notebooks and 6 pens is ₹333. Find the cost of one notebook.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Difference** in the number of **notebooks** = 7 − 4 = 3 notebooks.

Since the number of **pens** is the same (6 in both cases), the **price difference** is solely due to these 3 notebooks.

**Price difference** = ₹ 333 − ₹ 228 = ₹ 105.

**Cost of 1 notebook** = 105 ÷ 3 = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost** of **4 notebooks** and **6 pens** = **₹ 228**

**Cost** of **7 notebooks** and **6 pens** = **₹ 333**

**Formula Used:**

The **Elimination Method** for solving a **System of Linear Equations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b93a2f26038cf99371ab54e955b2dc732ed62a4f51b78bf486cbd3cf331d4f6d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **cost** of one **notebook** be N and the **cost** of one **pen** be P.

⇒ 4N + 6P = 228 — (Equation 1)

⇒ 7N + 6P = 333 — (Equation 2)

⇒ Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ (7N + 6P) − (4N + 6P) = 333 − 228

⇒ (7N − 4N) + (6P − 6P) = 105

⇒ 3N = 105

⇒ N = 105 ÷ 3

questions.question: A parallelogram has sides 12 cm and 9 cm long. The length of one of its diagonals is 15 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the parallelogram?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A **diagonal** divides a **parallelogram** into two **congruent triangles**.

The sides of the triangle are 9 cm, 12 cm, and 15 cm.

Recognize the **Pythagorean triplet**: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15².

Since it is a **right-angled triangle**, the area of the parallelogram is simply the product of its adjacent sides.

Area = 12 cm × 9 cm = 108 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 108 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Adjacent sides of the **parallelogram** are **a = 12 cm** and **b = 9 cm**. Length of the **diagonal** is **d = 15 cm**.

**Formula Used:** Area of parallelogram = 2 × Area of the triangle formed by its sides and diagonal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28030b74a331e2f174118a3179c305a86f926094f6a778bef03176799ba7da5b.png] 

⇒ Let the triangle be ΔABC with sides 9 cm, 12 cm, and 15 cm.

⇒ Checking for a **right-angled triangle**: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225.

⇒ Square of the longest side (diagonal) = 15² = 225.

⇒ Since 9² + 12² = 15², the triangle is **right-angled** at the vertex between sides 9 cm and 12 cm.

⇒ Area of ΔABC = 1 ÷ 2 × base × height = 1 ÷ 2 × 12 × 9 = 54 cm².

⇒ Area of **parallelogram** = 2 × Area of ΔABC = 2 × 54 = 108 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 108 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Parallelogram Diagonals

Each **diagonal** of a **parallelogram** divides it into two **triangles** of **equal area**.

Heron's Formula

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c)], where s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Parallelogram Law

The sum of the squares of the four sides of a **parallelogram** is equal to the sum of the squares of its two **diagonals**: 2(a² + b²) = d₁² + d₂².

questions.question: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act of which year, every State / District Authority or the Supreme Court / High Court Legal Services Committee or Taluk Legal Services Committee may organise Lok Adalats, as the case may be?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1987**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987** was enacted by the Parliament to provide a statutory base to legal aid programs and to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
 
• Under **Section 19** of the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**, the **State Authority**, **District Authority**, **Supreme Court Legal Services Committee**, **High Court Legal Services Committee**, or **Taluk Legal Services Committee** are empowered to organize **Lok Adalats**.
 
• The Act defines the **Lok Adalat** as a forum where disputes or cases pending in the court of law or at the pre-litigation stage are settled or compromised amicably.
 
• The legislation was a direct result of the constitutional mandate under **Article 39A**, which requires the State to provide **free legal aid** and ensure equal justice.
 
• Every award made by a **Lok Adalat** is deemed to be a decree of a civil court or an order of any other court and is final and binding on all parties to the dispute.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 39A of the Indian Constitution**:

 
 
• It was inserted by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• It directs the State to provide **free legal aid** by suitable legislation or schemes to ensure that justice is not denied due to economic or other disabilities.
 
 
 
• **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)**:
 
 
• It was constituted under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987** to monitor and evaluate the implementation of legal aid programs.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** serves as the **Patron-in-Chief**, and the second senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is the **Executive Chairman**.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction of Lok Adalats**:
 
 
• They can deal with **compoundable civil, revenue, and criminal cases**.
 
• They do not have jurisdiction over matters relating to an offense **not compoundable** under any law.

questions.question: Which of the following desert features forms due to parallel retreat of slopes through backwasting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pediplain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Pediplain** is a broad, low-relief erosional surface formed in **arid** and **semi-arid** regions through the coalescence of several **pediments**.
 
• The concept was famously developed by the geomorphologist **L.C. King** in the mid-20th century as part of his **Cycle of Pediplanation**, which serves as an alternative to **W.M. Davis's** peneplanation theory.
 
• The fundamental mechanism behind this formation is the **parallel retreat of slopes**, also known as **scarp retreat** or **backwasting**, where the steep face of a mountain or upland recedes horizontally while maintaining a constant angle.
 
• As the mountain front or scarp moves backward due to **weathering** and **sheetwash**, it leaves behind a gently inclined bedrock platform known as a **pediment** at its base.
 
• Over vast geological timescales, the continuous **backwasting** causes these pediments to expand and eventually merge, resulting in a vast, multi-concave plain that may contain isolated remnant hills called **Inselbergs** or **Bornhardts**.
 
• Unlike **peneplanation**, which relies on **down-wasting** (vertical reduction of height), pediplanation is driven by **lateral erosion** and the horizontal migration of slope profiles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blowout**:

 
 
• Commonly known as **deflation hollows**, these are depressions formed in sandy deserts where **aeolian** (wind) processes remove loose, non-cohesive sediments.
 
• They can range from a few meters to several kilometers in diameter and are strictly products of **wind erosion** rather than slope retreat.
 
 
 
• **Stalagmite**:
 
 
• A type of **speleothem** or cave formation that grows upward from the floor of a limestone cavern.
 
• It is formed by the **precipitation** of calcium carbonate from mineral-rich water dripping from the ceiling, making it a primary feature of **Karst topography**.
 
 
 
• **Playa**:
 
 
• An exceptionally flat, dry lake bed located in the lowest part of an **undrained desert basin** (bolson).
 
• These surfaces are characterized by the accumulation of fine-grained silts, clays, and **evaporite minerals** like salt and gypsum after the evaporation of ephemeral floodwaters.

questions.question: Which of the following are the official languages of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindi and English**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 343(1)** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **official language** of the **Union** is **Hindi** written in the **Devanagari script**.
 
• The **Constitution** originally stipulated that **English** would continue to be used for all official purposes of the **Union** for a period of **15 years** from the commencement of the **Constitution** (i.e., until **1965**).
 
• To prevent administrative difficulties and address concerns from non-Hindi speaking regions, the **Official Languages Act, 1963** was passed, which permitted the continued use of **English** for official purposes alongside **Hindi** indefinitely.
 
• Currently, **Section 3** of the **Official Languages Act** ensures that **English** remains an **associate official language** for communication between the **Union** and states, as well as for parliamentary proceedings.
 
• It is important to note that India has no **National Language** defined by the **Constitution**; rather, it identifies **Hindi** and **English** as the languages for official executive and legislative transactions at the federal level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eighth Schedule of the Constitution**

 
 
• The **Eighth Schedule** lists **22 languages** that are given statutory recognition and encouragement, including **Urdu**, **Marathi**, **Bengali**, and **Sanskrit**.
 
• While **Urdu** and **Marathi** are **scheduled languages** and serve as **official languages** in specific states (like **Uttar Pradesh** or **Maharashtra**), they are not the **official languages** of the **Union of India**.
 
• The **Official Language Commission** is established under **Article 344** to make recommendations regarding the progressive use of **Hindi** for official purposes.
 
• **Article 348** specifies that the language of the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts**, as well as for Bills and Acts, shall be **English** until **Parliament** provides otherwise.

questions.question: Which outcome resulted from the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms)?

options.text: Establishment of provincial autonomy, complete financial authority, and autonomous ministries
Reduction of legislative council size, replacement of budgetary rights, and elimination of Indian representatives.
Expansion of legislative councils, admission of Indians to Viceroy's executive council, and new deliberative powers.
Abolition of nominated seats, imposition of direct elections, and removal of official majorities.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Expansion of legislative councils, admission of Indians to Viceroy's executive council, and new deliberative powers.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Councils Act of 1909**, popularly referred to as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, significantly increased the size of the legislative councils. The number of members in the **Central Legislative Council** was raised from **16 to 60**, while the number of members in the **Provincial Legislative Councils** of **Bengal**, **Madras**, and **Bombay** was also increased to **50** each.
 
• For the first time in British Indian history, the act provided for the association of **Indians** with the executive councils of the **Viceroy** and **Governors**. **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** was appointed as the first Indian member of the **Viceroy's Executive Council**, serving as the **Law Member**.
 
• The act substantially enlarged the **deliberative functions** of the legislative councils at both levels. Members were given the right to ask **supplementary questions**, move **resolutions on the budget**, and discuss matters of **public interest**, although the executive was not bound by these resolutions.
 
• While it allowed a **non-official majority** in the **Provincial Legislative Councils**, the act maintained an **official majority** in the **Central Legislative Council** to ensure British control over vital central legislation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Communal Representation**

 
 
• The act is most notable for introducing a system of **separate electorates** for **Muslims**. Under this provision, Muslim representatives were to be elected exclusively by Muslim voters, effectively legalizing communalism in Indian politics.
 
• **Lord Minto**, the then **Viceroy**, is consequently known as the **Father of Communal Electorate** due to this institutionalization of political division.
 
 
 
• **Distinction from Other Acts**
 
 
• **Provincial Autonomy**: This was a core feature of the **Government of India Act of 1935**, which granted provinces independent financial and administrative powers, unlike the 1909 Act which kept them subordinate.
 
• **Dyarchy**: The system of double government (reserved and transferred subjects) was introduced by the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms** (**Government of India Act of 1919**), not the 1909 Act.
 
• **Direct Elections**: The 1909 Act utilized a highly **indirect** and restricted system of election through local bodies and chambers of commerce; widespread **direct elections** were only introduced in subsequent reforms.

questions.question: Which innovation correctly illustrates Mesolithic advances in subsistence and technology in India?

options.text: Adoption of iron tools indicates an early transition to metal-using cultures
Emergence of polished stone axes associated with settled agricultural villages
Manufacture of heavy flake tools similar to Lower Paleolithic hand-axes
Use of microlithic tools along with bow-and-arrow and plant-processing implements

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Use of microlithic tools along with bow-and-arrow and plant-processing implements**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mesolithic period** in India (approximately **10,000 BCE to 4,000 BCE**) marks a significant transition from the **Paleolithic** hunter-gatherer lifestyle to a more specialized subsistence pattern during the early **Holocene** epoch.
 
• The defining technological advancement of this era was the production of **microliths**, which are tiny, geometric stone tools (1 to 8 cm in length) crafted from crypto-crystalline silica like **chert**, **agate**, **jasper**, and **chalcedony**.
 
• These **microliths** were rarely used alone; instead, they were **hafted** into bone or wooden handles to create sophisticated **composite tools** such as **sickles**, **saws**, and **barbed spears**.
 
• A critical innovation in hunting technology was the **bow and arrow**, which enabled Mesolithic humans to hunt smaller, agile animals and birds, a necessity as the post-glacial climate led to the growth of forests and changed the local fauna.
 
• Archaeological excavations at sites like **Bagor** in Rajasthan and **Adamgarh** in Madhya Pradesh have unearthed **plant-processing implements** such as **grindstones**, **querns**, and **rubbers**, indicating the systematic gathering and processing of wild grains and seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other historical stages:
 
 
• **Iron tools**: These appeared much later during the **Iron Age** (circa **1000 BCE** in India), facilitating the clearing of dense forests in the **Gangetic Valley**.
 
• **Polished stone axes**: These are the hallmark of the **Neolithic Age**, where the shift to **settled agriculture**, **animal domestication**, and the use of **pottery** became prevalent.
 
• **Heavy flake tools**: Tools like **hand-axes** and **cleavers** are characteristic of the **Lower Paleolithic** (Acheulean culture), designed for heavy-duty tasks like butchering and digging.

questions.question: High sea waves triggered by an undersea earthquake are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tsunamis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Tsunami** is a series of powerful waves caused by a large and sudden displacement of the ocean, most commonly triggered by an **undersea earthquake** along **tectonic plate** boundaries.
 
• When an earthquake occurs beneath the ocean floor, the sudden vertical movement of the **seafloor** displaces a massive volume of water, creating energy that radiates outward in the form of **long-period waves**.
 
• In the deep ocean, tsunamis can travel at speeds of up to **800 kilometers per hour** (equivalent to the speed of a jet aircraft) while maintaining a very long **wavelength**, often making them nearly unnoticeable on the surface.
 
• As these waves approach shallow coastal waters, they undergo **shoaling**; the wave speed decreases due to friction with the rising seabed, causing the **wave height** to increase significantly, often resulting in a wall of water.
 
• The term is derived from the Japanese words **tsu** (meaning harbor) and **nami** (meaning wave), as these waves frequently cause devastating impacts in coastal harbors and low-lying areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glacial Surges**:

 
 
• These are short-lived events during which a **glacier** advances at speeds significantly faster than its normal rate, sometimes up to **10 to 100 times** faster.
 
• They are primarily driven by **internal hydrological changes** or basal lubrication rather than seismic activity under the sea.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Winds**:
 
 
• These are **seasonal reversing winds** accompanied by corresponding changes in **precipitation**, most notably affecting the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
 
• They are caused by the differential heating of **land and water** rather than geological shifts in the earth's crust.
 
 
 
• **Land Depressions**:
 
 
• In a meteorological context, a **depression** refers to a region of **low atmospheric pressure** that often results in stormy or unsettled weather.
 
• In geology, it refers to a **sunken area** or basin formed by erosion, tectonic activity, or **subsidence**.

questions.question: In physical science, understanding the dimension of a quantity helps to analyze formulas and relationships between variables. Which set of dimensions correctly represents the physical quantity 'force' in terms of mass, length, and time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mass times length times time^-2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In physics, **Force** is defined by **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, which mathematically states that force is the product of **mass** (m) and **acceleration** (a).
 
• The physical dimensions of any quantity are expressed in terms of the fundamental dimensions: **Mass [M]**, **Length [L]**, and **Time [T]**.
 
• **Acceleration** is the rate of change of **velocity** with respect to **time**. Since velocity has the dimensions of **Length per unit Time** ([L][T]−¹), acceleration possesses the dimensions of [L][T]−¹ / [T], which simplifies to **[LT−²]**.
 
• By substituting these values into the force equation (Force = Mass × Acceleration), the dimensional formula is derived as [M] × [LT−²], resulting in **[MLT−²]**.
 
• This dimensional structure, **mass times length times time−²**, signifies that force is directly proportional to mass and distance but inversely proportional to the square of time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Units and Measurements**:

 
 
• The **SI unit** of force is the **Newton (N)**. One Newton is defined as the force needed to provide a mass of 1 **kilogram** with an acceleration of 1 **meter per second squared** (1 N = 1 kg·m/s²).
 
• In the **CGS (Centimeter-Gram-Second) system**, the unit of force is the **dyne**, where 1 Newton is equivalent to 10⁵ dynes.
 
 
 
• **Dimensional Analysis**:
 
 
• It is a crucial tool used to verify the **dimensional consistency** of physical equations, ensuring that both sides of an equation have identical dimensions.
 
• It helps in deriving relations between various physical quantities such as **Work** (Force × Displacement: [ML²T−²]) and **Pressure** (Force / Area: [ML−¹T−²]).
 
• Force is a **vector quantity**, characterized by both a **magnitude** and a **direction**, and its behavior is governed by the principles of **classical mechanics**.

questions.question: The President may return a non-money bill to Parliament for reconsideration for how many times?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Once only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 111** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President** has the authority to return a bill to **Parliament** for reconsideration, provided it is not a **Money Bill**.
 
• This executive power is commonly referred to as the **Suspensive Veto**, allowing the **President** to request the legislature to review specific clauses or the entire bill.
 
• The **Constitution** mandates that if the bill is passed again by both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**, with or without the amendments suggested by the **President**, and is presented again, the **President** must give their assent.
 
• Because the **President** is constitutionally obligated to sign the bill upon its second presentation, the right to return the legislation can be exercised **once only** for any specific bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exceptions to the Veto Power**:

 
 
• **Money Bills**: According to **Article 110**, a **Money Bill** cannot be returned for reconsideration. The **President** can either give assent or withhold it, but normally gives assent as it is introduced with their prior recommendation.
 
• **Constitutional Amendment Bills**: The **24th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1971** made it obligatory for the **President** to give assent to any bill seeking to amend the **Constitution** under **Article 368**.
 
 
 
• **Other Veto Types**:
 
 
• **Absolute Veto**: The power of the **President** to say 'no' to a bill passed by **Parliament**, after which the bill ends and does not become an **Act**.
 
• **Pocket Veto**: The **President** exercises this by keeping the bill pending on their desk for an indefinite period, neither giving assent nor returning it. This is possible because the **Indian Constitution** does not specify a time limit for the **President** to act on a bill.

questions.question: In which region of Gujarat are Duha, Sorathaa, Chaand, Belaads, etc. traditionally performed in folk music?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Saurashtra** region, also known as **Kathiyawad**, is the cultural epicenter for specific oral traditions and folk music forms like **Duha**, **Sorathaa**, and **Chhand**. These forms are deeply rooted in the **Charani literature** of the region. Hence, the region of **Saurashtra** is the correct context for these performances.
 
• **Duha** and **Sorathaa** are rhythmic poetic couplets that form the backbone of the **Lok Dayro**, a traditional community gathering where folk artists, often from the **Gadhavi** and **Charan** communities, recite heroic and moral verses. Hence, these are traditionally performed in the **Saurashtra** folk music style.
 
• The musical meters known as **Chhand** (such as **Savaiya** and **Bhujangi**) are used to narrate tales of bravery, spirituality, and nature, utilizing a distinct high-pitched and robust vocal delivery unique to the peninsula of **Gujarat**. Hence, these poetic structures are characteristic of **Saurashtra**.
 
• Renowned folk scholar **Jhaverchand Meghani**, titled the **Rashtriya Shayar**, extensively documented these forms in his seminal work **Saurashtra Ni Rasdhar**, highlighting their deep-seated connection to this specific geographical area. Hence, **Saurashtra** is the region where these are traditionally performed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding the Folk Forms:**

• Although the **Governor** is the appointing authority, the power to remove a member or the Chairman of the **SPSC** is vested exclusively in the **President of India** as per **Article 317**.
 
• The **President** can remove a member on the grounds of **misbehaviour** only after the **Supreme Court** has conducted an inquiry and recommended removal; the advice tendered by the **Supreme Court** is binding on the **President**.
 
• This constitutional provision ensures the **independence** and **impartiality** of the **SPSC** by protecting its members from arbitrary removal by the state executive or the **Chief Minister**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **President** can also remove a member without a **Supreme Court** inquiry if the member is adjudged an **insolvent**.
 
• Removal is applicable if the member engages in any **paid employment** outside the duties of their office during their term.
 
• If the member is, in the opinion of the **President**, unfit to continue in office by reason of **infirmity of mind or body**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with UPSC:**
 
 
• The **Chairman** and members of the **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** are both appointed and removed by the **President of India**.
 
• Members of a **Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC)**, created by an **Act of Parliament**, are also appointed and removed by the **President**.
 
 
 
• **Term of Office:**
 
 
• A member of the **SPSC** holds office for a term of **six years** or until they attain the age of **62 years**, whichever is earlier.

questions.question: If an object having a mass of 10 kg is moving with a velocity of 50 m/s, find the correct momentum of the object.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**500 kg m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Momentum** is defined in physics as the quantity of motion an object possesses, which is mathematically the product of its **mass** and **velocity**.
 
• The formula to calculate linear momentum is expressed as **p = m × v**, where **p** represents momentum, **m** is the mass of the object, and **v** is its velocity.
 
• In this specific problem, the **mass (m)** of the object is given as **10 kg** and the **velocity (v)** is provided as **50 m/s**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula, we get: **p = 10 kg × 50 m/s**, which equals **500 kg m/s**.
 
• Since momentum is the product of mass in **kilograms** and velocity in **meters per second**, the resulting **SI unit** is **kg m/s** (kilogram-meter per second).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical Characteristics of Momentum:**

 
 
• **Vector Quantity:** Momentum is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both magnitude and direction. The direction of the momentum vector is always the same as the direction of the **velocity vector**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional representation of momentum is **[M L T−¹]**, derived from mass [M] and velocity [L T−¹].
 
• **Newton's Second Law:** This law states that the **force** applied to an object is equal to the rate of change of its momentum over time (F = dp/dt).
 
• **Conservation of Momentum:** This fundamental principle asserts that in the absence of external forces, the **total momentum** of a closed system remains constant during interactions or collisions.
 
• **Impulse:** The change in momentum is also known as **impulse**, which is the product of the average force and the time interval over which it acts.

questions.question: The Capability Approach, which defines development as expanding individuals’ freedoms, was first proposed by which economist?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amartya Sen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Capability Approach** is a normative framework developed by the Indian economist and philosopher **Amartya Sen** in the 1980s, primarily to evaluate individual well-being and social arrangements.
 
• Unlike traditional economic models that focus on **utility** or **income (GDP)**, Sen’s approach emphasizes **substantive freedom**—the actual ability of people to achieve the things they value doing and being.
 
• Sen distinguished between **functionings** (the actual states of being and doing, such as being healthy or literate) and **capabilities** (the set of alternative combinations of functionings that are feasible for a person to achieve).
 
• This paradigm shift influenced global development policy, providing the conceptual foundation for the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, which was launched by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in 1990.
 
• Amartya Sen was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences** in **1998** for his contributions to **welfare economics** and his work on famine and human development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Martha Nussbaum**:

 
 
• A prominent American philosopher who collaborated with Sen but diverged by proposing a specific list of **Ten Central Human Capabilities** (e.g., life, bodily health, practical reason) as a requirement for social justice.
 
 
 
• **John Rawls**:
 
 
• An influential political philosopher known for his work **A Theory of Justice** (1971); while his concept of **primary goods** influenced Sen, Sen critiqued Rawls for focusing too much on the distribution of resources rather than what individuals can actually do with those resources.
 
 
 
• **Adam Smith**:
 
 
• Known as the **Father of Modern Economics** and author of **The Wealth of Nations** (1776); although he focused on market mechanisms, Sen often cited Smith's observations on **necessaries** and social participation as early precursors to the capability perspective.

questions.question: What major change was made to the Right to Property by the 44th Amendment Act (1978)?

options.text: It was removed from Fundamental Rights
It was elevated to a Directive Principle
It was given more enforcement power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It was removed from Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** of **1978** officially removed the **Right to Property** from the list of **Fundamental Rights** (Part III) of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• Before this amendment, the right to property was guaranteed under **Article 19(1)(f)** and **Article 31**.
 
• Post-amendment, it was reclassified as a **Legal Right** or **Constitutional Right** and placed under a new **Article 300A** in **Part XII**.
 
• The primary purpose of this change was to prevent the **judiciary** from blocking **land reforms** and social welfare legislation aimed at the **equitable distribution** of resources.
 
• As a result of being a legal right rather than a fundamental one, a citizen cannot approach the **Supreme Court** directly under **Article 32** for its violation, though they can still seek relief through **High Courts** under **Article 226**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 300A**:

 
 
• It specifies that no person shall be deprived of their property except by **authority of law**, meaning the state must follow a legislative process to acquire land.
 
• It provides protection against arbitrary **executive action** but does not offer the same level of immunity against **legislative action** as a fundamental right.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights vs. Legal Rights**:
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights** (Articles 12 to 35) are considered essential for the development of individuals and are protected by the **Basic Structure** doctrine.
 
• **Legal Rights** are protected by ordinary law and can be modified by the **Parliament** through regular legislative procedures.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**:
 
 
• Articles **39(b)** and **39(c)** direct the state to ensure that the ownership and control of material resources are distributed to serve the **common good**, which often conflicted with the earlier status of property as a fundamental right.

questions.question: What do we call the lasting of sound caused by repeated reflections?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reverberation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reverberation** refers to the persistence of sound in a particular space after the original sound source has stopped. It is primarily caused by **multiple reflections** of sound waves from various surfaces like walls, ceilings, and floors.
 
• When sound is produced in a large enclosed area, such as an **auditorium** or a **concert hall**, the sound waves bounce back and forth, creating a continuous "smearing" effect where the sound lingers before eventually being absorbed.
 
• Scientific measurement of this phenomenon is known as **reverberation time**, which is the time required for the sound intensity to drop by **60 decibels** (dB) from its initial level.
 
• While a moderate amount of reverberation adds **richness** to music, excessive reverberation can cause **acoustic interference**, making speech unintelligible as syllables overlap with one another.
 
• To control this effect, engineers use **sound-absorbent materials** such as acoustic tiles, **fiberglass**, or heavy curtains to reduce the number of reflections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Echo**:

 
 
• An echo is a **distinct reflection** of sound that reaches the listener after a time delay of at least **0.1 seconds**.
 
• For a human ear to distinguish an echo from the original sound, the reflecting surface must be at a minimum distance of approximately **17.2 meters** (assuming the speed of sound is 344 m/s).
 
 
 
• **Resonance**:
 
 
• This is a physical phenomenon where a system oscillates with **maximum amplitude** at a specific **natural frequency**.
 
• It occurs when the frequency of a periodically applied force matches the system's own inherent frequency of vibration.
 
 
 
• **Quality**:
 
 
• Also referred to as **Timbre**, this property allows the human ear to distinguish between two sounds that have the same **pitch** and **loudness**.
 
• It depends on the **waveforms** and the presence of **overtones** or harmonics unique to a specific instrument or voice.

questions.question: When a metal spoon is placed in a hot cup of tea, it soon becomes warm. Which mode of heat transfer is primarily responsible for this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Conduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Conduction** is the primary mode of heat transfer in solids, where thermal energy is moved through a material by **direct molecular collision** without the actual movement of the matter itself.
 
• When a **metal spoon** is placed in **hot tea**, the faster-moving molecules of the tea collide with the atoms of the spoon, transferring **kinetic energy** to them.
 
• Metals are superior **thermal conductors** because they contain **free electrons** (delocalized electrons) that can move rapidly through the metal lattice, carrying thermal energy much faster than atomic vibrations alone.
 
• The process continues as the vibrating atoms at the submerged end of the spoon pass their energy to adjacent, cooler atoms through **intermolecular interactions**, a process that continues until the **handle** reaches a higher temperature.
 
• This transfer typically occurs from a region of **higher temperature** to a region of **lower temperature**, following the **Second Law of Thermodynamics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convection**:

 
 
• This mode occurs only in **fluids** (liquids and gases) and involves the actual movement of particles.
 
• In the tea itself, **convection currents** form as the warmer, less dense liquid rises and the cooler, denser liquid sinks.
 
 
 
• **Radiation**:
 
 
• Energy is transferred via **electromagnetic waves** (specifically infrared radiation) and does not require a physical medium.
 
• While the cup and tea emit **thermal radiation**, it is not the primary reason the handle of the submerged spoon heats up so quickly.
 
 
 
• **Insulation**:
 
 
• Refers to the use of materials with low **thermal conductivity**, such as wood, plastic, or cork.
 
• These **insulators** are used to prevent or slow down the rate of heat transfer, which is why handles of cooking pans are often made of plastic or wood rather than **conductive metal**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly highlights the primary difference between System Software and Application Software?

options.text: System software is developed by large companies, while application software is developed only by individual programmers.
System software manages the computer's core resources and provides a platform for other programs, while application software is designed to perform specific tasks for the user.
System software is always free and open-source, but application software must always be purchased with a license.
Application software is required to start the computer, whereas system software is used only after the computer has fully booted up.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**System software manages the computer's core resources and provides a platform for other programs, while application software is designed to perform specific tasks for the user.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **System software** is a type of computer program designed to run a computer's hardware and **application programs**. It serves as the interface between the **hardware** and the user.
 
• The primary purpose of system software is to manage the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **memory**, and **peripheral devices** like printers and disk drives. Examples include **Operating Systems (OS)** such as **Windows**, **Linux**, and **macOS**.
 
• **Application software**, often referred to as 'apps' or end-user programs, is designed to perform specific tasks for the user. These include **Word Processors**, **Web Browsers**, and **Database Management Systems**.
 
• While system software runs in the background and is essential for the computer to function, application software is used only when a user needs to complete a particular job, like editing a photo or browsing the **Internet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **System Software Categories**:

 
 
• **Operating Systems**: Provides the **User Interface (UI)** and manages system resources.
 
• **Device Drivers**: Specialized programs that allow the OS to communicate with specific hardware like **Graphic Cards**.
 
• **Utility Software**: Programs used for maintenance, such as **Antivirus** or **Disk Defragmenters**.
 
 
 
• **Application Software Types**:
 
 
• **General Purpose**: Software like **Microsoft Excel** used for various broad tasks.
 
• **Customized Software**: Tailor-made programs for specific organizational needs, such as **Banking Software** or **Railway Reservation Systems**.
 
 
 
• **Booting Process**: System software, specifically the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** and the **Kernel**, is required to start the computer. Application software cannot run until the system software has finished the **booting** sequence.

questions.question:
Vimal ranked 28th from the top and 65th from the bottom in his class.

How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

 
• **Position of Vimal from the top** = 28th
 
• **Position of Vimal from the bottom** = 65th

**Total number of students** = (Position of a person from the top + Position of the same person from the bottom) − 1

**Total number of students** = (28 + 65) − 1

= 93 − 1

= 92

So, there are **92 students** in the class.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 1'**.
